label: CPU saturation alert
description: CPU 97% with throttling; error rate only 4.1% because requests are throttled, not failed.

evidence.title: catalog-api: CPU saturation 97%, category pages degraded
evidence.detail: Category and product pages take 4-9s. CPU 97% (baseline 34%), queries-per-request 1180 (baseline 9), error rate 4.1%. Monitor: catalog_api.cpu_saturation{service=catalog-api}.

evidence.title: catalog-api v5.2.0 deployed 11 minutes before the alert
evidence.detail: Serializer rewrite: removed ProductVariant prefetch, lazy-load variants per item. Deployed by @t.nguyen, 21 files changed, flagged high risk.

evidence.title: catalog-api degraded; postgres-catalog degraded; redis healthy
evidence.detail: catalog-api status=degraded (CPU). postgres-catalog status=degraded, CPU 96%, 41k queries/min (baseline 900). redis-cache healthy 1.3ms p95.

hint: CPU plus query volume, not timeouts. Check queries-per-request before restarting anything.

label: N+1 query storm identified
description: The serializer executes a query per item; 71% of CPU is row hydration.

evidence.title: N+1 detected: 1180 queries for one category page (baseline 9)
evidence.detail: per-item query executed for cart_items_query, lazy load in the serializer. Profile shows 71% of CPU in ORM row hydration for ProductVariant.

evidence.title: Postgres CPU 96% with 41k queries/min from catalog-api
evidence.detail: Database load is a side effect of our own query volume (41k/min vs 900/min baseline); the database is not independently failing.

hint: The database is a symptom here. Rolling back the serializer change is the structural fix.

label: Restart mitigation applied
description: Reachable only by executing the restart action. 25 second CPU dip.

evidence.title: After rolling restart: CPU 41% for 25s, then 97% again
evidence.detail: Workers restarted onto the same v5.2.0 build. CPU dipped to 41% and returned to 97% within 30 seconds; queries-per-request unchanged at 1180.

hint: The restart did not change the query shape. That is the definition of a symptom-only mitigation.

label: Service recovered
description: Rollback restored the prefetch; CPU and query volume back to baseline.

evidence.title: Resolved: CPU 31%, 11 queries/request, page p95 230ms
evidence.detail: catalog-api rolled back to v5.1.4 with the ProductVariant prefetch restored. DB queries/min back to 940, postgres CPU 24%.

hint: Stable. Retain the lesson: query volume is the first thing to check on a CPU incident, and scaling out is the wrong reflex.
